title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
abstract: arXiv:2610.42030v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged. Unfortunately, every generated token pays for the loop. Re-applying m of N layers makes each token about (N+m)/N times as expensive. Loops that a model learns during large-scale pretraining justify this price, but whether loops added after pretraining justify this cost remains unclear. We compare a looped model with two simple baselines. We first compare it with the same model trained identically without the loop (equal parameters). Secondly, we compare it with the best unlooped use of the same inference floating-point operations (equal FLOPs). tldr: 在已训练模型上添加循环虽不增加参数量与训练成本，但会推高每个token的推理计算量；在0.8B至9B的Qwen3和Qwen3.5模型实验中，只有最小的0.8B循环模型能同时超越参数量相同和FLOPs相同的两个基线，说明预训练后加循环仅在极小模型上划算。
en_tdlr: Looping a trained model leaves parameters and training cost unchanged but raises per-token inference compute, and across Qwen3/3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B only the 0.8B looped model beats both equal-parameter and equal-FLOPs baselines.
